title: Scout S2: kgpt github module and kernel github.py — import and commit flows, what refresh, diff, lazy read and pull request need
spec: Read-only scout over /Users/k3ntaw/code/kgpt. Read modules/github/server.py, modules/github/api.py, modules/github/module.yaml, kernel/kgpt_kernel/github.py, modules/github/tests/*, and docs/handbook/15-github.md. Report: (1) the import flow step by step: which GitHub endpoints (tree, blob), what is stored per file (path, folder, sha?) and what is dropped; (2) commit_files: which endpoints, how the branch is created from base, what happens if the branch exists, size limits; (3) how the App auth works (installation token minting, required permissions) and what extra permission a pull request needs; (4) the gaps for: refresh_repo (compare tree shas against stored ones), per-file diff (is the base blob sha or content kept anywhere?), lazy single-file read from the repo, propose_pull_request, listing branches; (5) the module contract rules a new tool must follow (tier, untrusted flag, ceiling) from module.yaml comments and modules/_template. (6) how the module tests mock the GitHub API so new tools can be tested the same way. Cite path:line, one confidence per finding. Do not read the web client.
acceptance: Result documents import and commit flows with endpoints and path:line citations
Result states what per-file provenance is stored today and what is missing for refresh and diff
Result lists the new tools needed with proposed tier and untrusted flag, and how to test them with the existing mocks

findings.claim: Import flow: read_repo_tree/import_repo call api.tree() -> GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/git/trees/{ref}?recursive=1, keeping only blob entries as {path, size, sha}; a truncated GitHub response is surfaced as a synthetic entry rather than hidden

import_repo filters tree entries with kernel worth_importing() (skips .git/node_modules/.venv/venv/__pycache__/dist/build/.next/target dirs, dotfiles except .gitignore/.env.example, and files over 2MB), fetches bytes per kept file via api.blob() -> GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/git/blobs/{sha}, then hands (path, bytes) tuples to kernel import_into_project which stores each as an attachment and mirrors the repo's folder structure

Per-file, only the attribution string 'imported from {owner}/{repo}@{ref}' is stored (via store.save's attribution field); the blob sha, the file size from the tree, and the tree/commit sha of the import are all dropped after the import completes — nothing persists the GitHub-side identity of an imported file

import_repo caps at MAX_FILES=400 files and MAX_TOTAL_BYTES=40MB per import, MAX_FILE_BYTES=2MB per file, and reports 'stopped_at_limit' rather than silently truncating when eligible files exceed the file-count cap

commit_files: mints an installation token (POST /app/installations/{id}/access_tokens), reads the base branch tip (GET /repos/{o}/{r}/git/ref/heads/{base}) and its commit's tree sha (GET /repos/{o}/{r}/git/commits/{parent}), creates one blob per file (POST .../git/blobs), one tree built on base_tree (POST .../git/trees), one commit with parents=[parent] (POST .../git/commits), then a brand-new ref (POST .../git/refs, ref=refs/heads/{branch}) — six calls total, order pinned by test

The branch is always created fresh off base's current tip (never PATCHed); if the branch already exists, POST .../git/refs simply fails and surfaces as GitHubSaidNo — there is no pre-check, no merge, and no fallback path for 'branch exists'

commit_files enforces no size limits of its own (no file count or byte cap) — server.py's propose_commit only validates branch!=base, a non-empty message, and a non-empty files list, unlike import_repo's explicit MAX_FILES/MAX_FILE_BYTES/MAX_TOTAL_BYTES

App auth: JWT signed RS256 from GITHUB_APP_PRIVATE_KEY, iat backdated 60s, exp = 9 minutes; installation_token() exchanges it for an ~hour-long token per call and is deliberately never cached (to honor revocation immediately)

Required App permissions per the handbook setup: Contents Read-and-write, Metadata Read-only, and optionally Administration Read-and-write (org-only) for create_repo — no Pull-requests permission is requested anywhere, so a propose_pull_request tool would need a new App permission ('Pull requests: Read and write') not currently part of setup

open_questions: Is there a separate kernel-level tier/autonomy enforcement file (referenced as '§6.5' and 'the tier system' in comments) that defines READ/READ_EXTERNAL/WRITE_LOCAL/WRITE_EXTERNAL semantics authoritatively, beyond what's inferable from module.yaml comments and server.py docstrings?
Does store.save (kernel/kgpt_kernel/documents/store.py) have a schema column that could hold a GitHub blob sha without a migration, or would refresh/diff require a new table?
suggested_next: New tools should be added as: refresh_repo (READ_EXTERNAL, untrusted) diffing tree() shas against a newly-added per-file sha column; read_repo_file (READ_EXTERNAL, untrusted) wrapping tree()+blob() for lazy single-file reads; list_branches (READ_EXTERNAL, untrusted) via GET /repos/{o}/{r}/branches; propose_pull_request (WRITE_EXTERNAL) via POST /repos/{o}/{r}/pulls, gated behind approval like propose_commit and requiring the App's Pull-requests permission to be added in the handbook setup steps
Persist blob sha (and ideally ref-at-import-time) per imported file — currently dropped — before attempting refresh_repo or diff, since there is nothing to compare against today

Test new endpoint-calling functions by extending or cloning the FakeGitHub pattern in test_commit.py (monkeypatch api._call), and add source-invariant assertions to test_github_api.py for any new interpolated path segment
